main_text.l: 14. De Fœdere.
SCoti isti Presbyterales haud vulgari Auxi-
liorum stipendio invitandi, nullo alio pre-
tio in partes trahuntur quam animarum
pignore posito, Ipsis scilicet qui illos evo-
cabant, Solenni Pacto & Fædere constri-
ctis.
Multæ hîc piæ Machinæ, & Religiosi
prætextus afferuntur ad oppugnandum Epis-
copatum vel prorsus demoliendum. Hunc
nempe Grandem Illum Cacodæmona, quem
(terriculamentis nonnullis adjectis) odio
vulgi, & pavoribus objiciunt, Solenni Car-
mine & Exorcismo ex Ecclesia omni modo
abigendum; postquam eam mille annos ob-
sederit, ex quo primo Christianismus in hac In-
sula plantatus, quique præscripto Universa-
si temporis simul & præxeos [?]in cæteris omni-
bus Ecclesiis, usque ab Apostolorum sæcu-
lo, ad hanc proximam Centuriam, inni-
titur.
Sed frustra caufam hic agit Antiquitas:
Presbyterismus velut adolescens hæres, nimis diu
Patrem vixisse ratus, & Episcopalis Cathe-

page.notes: Running head is Greek; the printed form reads ΒΑΣΙΑΙΚΗ (with Α where Λ is expected), kept as printed. "Universa-si" at the line end: the second part is unclear, read as "si" with [?]. "præxeos sin" in the line: "sin" is doubtful, read as printed with [?]; likely "in". Long s is set as plain s throughout. The heading's "Fœdere" is read from the scan as "Foedere" in the top line; body uses "Fædere". Paragraph 3 ends mid-word at "Cathe-" and the catchword "drae," belongs to the next page.
